cities.d: (กรุงเทพมหานคร) — Thailand's bustling, frenetic capital, known among the Thai as Krung Thep

x.around: Bangkok has a decent public transportation network by Southeast Asian standards, but much room for improvement lies in its integration. Bangkok is notorious for its traffic jams, so visitors are advised to rely on the rail and river networks whenever possible. Transit Bangkok is a journey planner that can help you choose the best route.

hidden.d: The largest aquarium in Southeast Asia, exhibiting over 30,000 marine animals from all over the world and featuring a wide range of rare and exotic species.
See the mingling of Arab and Thai cultures in this dense Arab neighborhood by Nana station. The area is flush with tourists from across the Arab world.
Located in front of Lumphini Park, the statue was sculpted by Professor Corado Feroci, an Italian sculptor that in Thailand is better known as Silpa Bhirasri.

A coffee shop with a Museum of Sex, devoted to the history of eroticism and the sex industry in Thailand. The proprietor's father, a wealthy property developer, has a larger sex museum, Kamavijitra, on Sukhumvit Soi 38.

n.en: Green Lantern Cafe and Sex Museum

hidden.d: This institute contains a collection of poisonous snakes which are "milked" daily for their venom in order to produce invaluable anti-snakebite serum.

n.en: Queen Saovabha Memorial Institute Snake Farm

hidden.d: The English-speaking international church community residing in the church actually dates from the 19th century, when the first Protestant missionaries came to Bangkok.
The highest observation deck in Thailand is located on the roof of Thailand's second-tallest skyscraper (314 meters, 78 floors) and offers a 360-degree panoramic city view.
A Hindu shrine that houses a statue of Phra Phrom, the Thai representation of the Hindu creation god Brahma.

x.intro: Bangkok (Thai: กรุงเทพฯ Krung Thep) is the capital and largest city of Thailand. With a population of over eleven million inhabitants, Bangkok is by far Thailand's main city, with the urban sprawl comprising nearly half of Thailand's population, and the largest city on the Southeast Asian mainland. Its high-rise buildings, heavy traffic congestion, intense heat and naughty nightlife do not immediately give you a warm welcome — but don't let your first impression mislead you.

must.d: The National Museum took over the Front Palace grounds, a former royal palace built in the 18th century just like the Grand Palace. The grounds are attractive in parts, but a bit sprawling and difficult to navigate.
A rare expanse of public greenery in the heart of the city, it was once property of King Rama VI, who issued a royal command to turn the area into a public park as a gift to Bangkok's residents.
This wat is becoming more and more off the beaten path as it is quite hard to walk here from the Grand Palace. Wat Suthat is huge and actually one of the most important temples for the Thai people.

n.en: Wat Suthat and the Giant Swing

must.d: The Assumption Cathedral is the main Roman Catholic church of Bangkok. The original building at this place was the brainchild of French missionary Father Pascal in 1809, and completed in 1821.
Visitors can interact with different kinds of arts, such as performance arts, music, painting and film, in various ways. On display are more than 300 works by Thai and international artists.

n.fr: Centre Culturel et Artistique de Bangkok

must.d: When the Thailand Tobacco Monopoly moved all its factory operations to Chiang Rai in 2008, the lake and some adjoining land that were part of its compound, previously enjoying semi-wild vegetation, were turned into a public park.
Now the central building of the National Museum, the Front Palace used to be an enormous complex stretching from the Chao Phraya River across Sanam Luang to Lot Canal.

Portuguese descendants of the early traders in Ayutthaya first settled at the other bank of the river in Thonburi (at the site of the Santa Cruz Church), but gradually moved to the opposite bank of the river.

next.d: interesting floating market popular with the locals
ancient capital showcasing its many ruins, 1.5 hr away by bus or train
its magnificent Summer Palace makes for a pleasant day trip
picture-perfect floating market on tourist steroids
beach resort town with nearby waterfalls and national parks
the famous Bridge over the River Kwai, the Erawan Falls and Hellfire Pass
rustic island to the north of Bangkok renowned for pottery making, a pleasant day trip out of the concrete jungle
Thailand's oldest city and site of the world's largest stupa

x.safe: Given its size, Bangkok is surprisingly safe, with violent crimes like mugging and robbery unusual. Most violent crime in Bangkok is connected to disputes between organized crime syndicates; if you do not bother them, they generally will not bother you. Generally speaking, the tourists who get into trouble are the ones who get into drunken fights.

cities.d: (พระนครศรีอยุธยา) — a historical city, UNESCO World Heritage Site and old capital of Siam (full name is Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya)

x.around: Cycling around the ruins is the most enjoyable way to spend the day. The archaeological park is easily reachable and manageable on bike even if you aren't very fit. The paths are paved and the distances between temples are short. You can rent a bicycle for around 40 baht/day.

hidden.d: A white and gold-coloured chedi built as a memorial to a previous queen. Set in small, well-kept gardens, it is the memorial for the first heroine in Siamese history.
Burial place of a Shiite Muslim historical figure who was the Minister of Civil Affairs under King Songtham (/1611-1628) of Siam.

An impressive building that houses a large cast-bronze Buddha image. It was originally enshrined outside the Grand Palace to the east, but it was later transferred to the current location and covered with a Mondop.

x.intro: Ayutthaya (Thai: อยุธยา), full name Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya (พระนครศรีอยุธยา), is an ancient capital and modern city in the Central Plains of Thailand, 85 north of Bangkok. Its proximity to Bangkok makes this city of 51,000 people (2020) a popular day-trip destination for travellers from that city.

must.d: The largest temple in Ayutthaya, known for its distinctive row of restored chedis (Thai-style stupas) found on many images of the city.
A large temple that was quite thoroughly ransacked by the Burmese. Several leaning prangs of Ayutthaya are still feebly defying gravity though, and the rows of headless Buddhas are atmospheric.

The temple that graces the official tourist pamphlet for Ayutthaya. King Prasat Thong commanded it built. Its great beauty has been reflected from the main stupa and its satellite stupas along the gallery, an architecture…
Bang Pa-In used to be a riverine island. When King Prasat Thong became the Ayutthaya king (1630–1655), he had the Chumphon Nikayaram Temple built on his family estate.
This temple stands out for having a large prang restored to its original condition, clearly visible if you come in from the east.

King Naresuan the Great commanded that the pagoda be built to celebrate the victory of his single-handed combat on elephant back. He also intended a huge construction to match the large pagoda of Wat Phukhao Thong.

n.en: Wat Yai Chaimongkon or Wat Chao Phraya Thai

must.d: Restored temple and monastery with ruined chedis. The main highlight is a 42-metre-long reclining Buddha, the only one of its kind on Ayutthaya island.
A working monastery south of Ayutthaya. No one knows how old it is, but it existed before Ayutthaya was founded as the capital.

next.d: famous for its eccentric palace and only 20 to the south
the famous bridge over the River Kwai and numerous World War II museums
first and 3rd largest national park of the country
the next destination if you take the train north, with monkeys and ancient ruins
gateway to the Isaan region
another former capital of Siam with impressive ancient ruins

x.safe: Ayutthaya has a lot of hungry stray dogs in poor condition. They can particularly be a problem in the off-season when there aren't so many people in the streets. While largely docile and harmless, to avoid being chased around by a pack of them it is best not to walk around alone, particularly at night. For those accustomed to travel in developing areas, there should be no problem.

cities.d: (เชียงใหม่) — de facto capital of Northern Thailand and the heart of Lanna culture

x.around: The traditional way of getting around the city is by songthaew (สองแถว) which serve as buses and taxis. These covered pick-up trucks have two long bench seats in the back (songthaew means "two rows" in Thai), the seats are shared by multiple passengers and the songthaews stop en route to pick up other passengers who are going the same way.

hidden.d: One of two money museums in Thailand, focused on northern Thailand, run by government treasury department, in a heritage building. It is small: plan 1 hr to see, need to take off shoes.
A huge lantern release (it is often referred to as the 10,000 lantern release, but there are not as many as that) happens near Mae Jo University on the Saturday before Loi Krathong,.
There are exhibitions by undergraduates from the Fine Arts Department at Chiang Mai University. These change often and the work on display is of high quality.
Community culture space that often hosts workshops like mini loom weaving or meditation.
Very nice temple with unusual architectural elements. Road 1269 is also part of the Samoeng Loop route.
Some buildings at the road, but turn left to go down to the actual temple. Nice views from the temple. The monk trail passes through the temple grounds.
Museum of stamps and postal related objects.
The museum is located on a little peninsula in a big pond. There is also an open air part to the museum at 300 m from the main building, where you find houses in the styles of the tribes.

x.intro: Chiang Mai (เชียงใหม่) is the hub of northern Thailand. On a plain at an elevation of 316 m, surrounded by mountains and lush countryside, it is much greener and quieter than the capital and has a cosmopolitan air and a significant expatriate population, all factors which have led many from Bangkok to settle permanently in this "rose of the north".

must.d: The quintessential image of Chiang Mai with its large gilded chedi, visible from the city on a clear day. Built in 1383 during the Lanna Thai period, legend has it that the temples site was selected by an elephant sent to roam…
Almost in the centre of Chiang Mai are the remains of a massive chedi that toppled in the great earthquake of 1545. The temple was originally constructed in 1401 on the orders of King Saeng Muang Ma.

Probably Chiang Mai's best-known temple, housing the Phra Singh image, completed between 1385 and 1400. Of most historical interest is the Wihan Lai Kham in the back, featuring Lanna-style temple murals and intricate gold…
The oldest temple in the city. Presumed to date from the year Chiang Mai was founded (1296), it is famed for two Buddha statues, which are about 1,800 and 1,000 years old, respectively.

A large park with over 400 species of animals, extremely popular with Thai tourists, and long queues may be encountered during Thai holidays. While better than some zoos, many animals are nevertheless kept in small enclosures.
The history and unusual architecture scattered under the yawning canopy of ancient trees is a pleasant antidote to the flash and bustle encountered at popular temples.

A large open-sided hall with a jumble of roughly hewn Buddhas with a huge dazzlingly whitewashed chedi behind. On the temple grounds is also a royal cemetery with the ashes collected from around Chiang Mai by princess Dara Rasmi…
Wat Lok Moli is a historic Lanna-style temple dating back to the 14th century.

next.d: an hour north of the city, and a good starting point for treks into the mountains
a relaxed city 3 hours north, and a transit point on the way to the Golden Triangle and Laos
the highest peak in Thailand (2,599 m), 60 km SW of Chiang Mai
urban Northern Thailand without the commercialism, 100 km SE of Chiang Mai
a scenic town with a long history and a longan festival, 26 km SE of Chiang Mai
20 minutes (15 km) north of the city with the Mae Sa valley leading to Samoeng and an interesting temple (Wat Pa Dara Phirom)
the former capital of a small kingdom filled with history and temples and surrounded by mountains

x.safe: The safest approach is to act like your Thai hosts and wear reasonable clothing (shoulders and chest covered) medium-length skirts, long shorts or long pants, speak in a moderate tone of voice, and avoid flashing money or jewellery. Not only will respectable Thais appreciate your behaviour, you are much less likely to become a target of any criminal activity.

cities.d: (เมืองเชียงราย) — gateway to the Golden Triangle, ethnic minorities and mountain treks

x.around: Public transport consists mainly of tuk-tuks and songthaews, plus a smaller number of taxis. However, most of the city itself, even the Blue Temple, can be explored on foot.

hidden.d: Small temple housing the spirit of the city (ming meuang) in an exquisitely carved and decorated Lanna-style, almost Laotian wiharn.
Built in 1914 at PratuSiri corner. It's Presbyterian.
A sizable fascinating pavilion dedicated to the life of the princess mother (grandmother of the present king, King Rama X).

This unique modern temple was designed and built by artist Chaloemchai Khositphiphat starting in 1998. A beautiful white ordination hall, Phra Ubosot, is decorated with silver glittering pieces of mirrors.

The collection displayes objects used in the royal courts such as Lanna, Khum Chao Phare, and Khum Chao Chiang Mai. Some are from northeast Myanmar, southwest China and Vietnam and are about 500-1,000 years old.
Used to house a major Buddha statue, the Phra Buddha Sihing, which is now enshrined in Chiang Mai. Like Wat Phra Kaeo, the temple now houses a replica instead.

Established through the cooperation of Mae Fa Luang University and the People’s Republic of China. The centre was built as a memorial to honour the princess mother as a symbol of friendship between the two nations.

n.en: Sirindhorns Chinese Language and Culture Centre

hidden.d: Large temple dedicated to Guan Yin (Avalokitesvara), with a 9-story pagoda and a 25-story giant statue.

x.intro: Chiang Rai (เชียงราย) is the capital of Chiang Rai Province, Northern Thailand.

must.d: Created by Thailand national artist, Thawan Duchanee, the grounds include nearly 40 small black houses made of wood, glass, concrete, bricks, or terracotta in various unique styles and design scattered around the temple’s area.

next.d: you can hire a car with driver for about 1,600 baht for the day, plus fuel, and you go where you want to go.
where Laos, Myanmar and Thailand meet, and formerly a major opium-growing region
and cross the Mekong to Huay Xai, Laos

cities.d: (หาดใหญ่) — the largest city in Southern Thailand, near the Malaysian border, and home to an eclectic mix of Southern Thais, Thai-Chinese and Malay Muslims

x.around: The city's "tourist center" is not far from the train station. It's quite compact and covers parts of the city's oldest roads: Nipat-u-thit (นิพัทธ์อุทิศ) 1, 2, and 3 Rd. Locals call these roads: Sai Nueng, Sai Song, Sai Saam (สายหนึ่ง, สายสอง, สายสาม; lit. Road One, Road Two, Road Three). It is practical to get around on foot, but getting to most attractions will require some kind of transportation.

hidden.d: There are two stations: one at Phra Buddha Mongkol Maharaj (พระพุทธมงคลมหาราช) and the other at Thao Maha Phrom (ท้าวมหาพรหม).
The park has two waterfalls: Ton Dat Fa and Ton Lat Fa.
mid-15 Dec through April.
This large, long man-made tunnel was once inhabited by Communist insurgents. It is three levels deep and contains several rooms. Entry fee for foreigners is 150 baht.

Home to staggering 287 bird species. The best time for bird watching and seeing a sea of blooming pink water lilies is during Jan-Apr. Go early in the morning to avoid strong sun. A boat ride costs 500 baht and takes about 1½ hr.
The waterfall is in the Ton Nga Chang Wildlife Sanctuary. It is one of the beautiful waterfalls in the south, about 26 km from the city. This waterfall has seven levels.
The first floating market in south Thailand. Sells mainly local foods.
This beautiful grand mosque is 400 m off the road from Hat Yai to Songkhla.

x.intro: Hat Yai (หาดใหญ่; also Hatyai, Had Yai, Haad Yai) is the fifth largest city in Thailand, the largest city in southern Thailand, and is in Songkhla Province on the Southern Gulf Coast. It's a popular tourist spot for Singaporeans, Indonesians, and especially Malaysians, as well as for Thais from neighbouring provinces. It's best avoided if you are looking to get off the beaten path. Prices are relatively high in tourist areas.

next.d: Thailand's bustling and vibrant capital city.
an artistic and cultural city in Northern Thailand; there are direct flights to Chiang Mai from Thai AirAsia.
There are 5 combined bus & speedboat services per day from Hat Yai Railway Station
One combined bus and boat service each day leaves Hat Yai Railway Station for Pak Bara pier where a speedboat will take you to Ko Tarutao.
Bangkok Airways used to fly direct: but Phantip travel runs a bus to Don Sak pier where ferries to the island can be boarded.
for beautiful islands such as Ko Lanta and Ko Phi Phi.
world-renowned white sandy beaches and resorts. Direct flights available with Bangkok Airways.
for the ferry to Langkawi

x.safe: A series of bombings from 2006 to 2012 that specifically targeted restaurants and shopping centres popular with visitors (and locals) killed two tourists. Strict security measures (bag searches, metal detectors) are to be expected in most gathering places. As of October 2022 the town is no more dangerous than any other major city in Thailand.

cities.d: (กาญจนบุรี) — home of the Bridge over the River Kwai and numerous World War II museums

x.around: Kanchanaburi is just a little too stretched out to comfortably walk. Small orange and large yellow songthaews (converted pickups) cruise up and down Saeng Chuto, connecting bus station, train station, and the bridge, and charge a standard 10 baht. Motorbike taxis and tuk-tuks are also available, with negotiable prices, and some guesthouses offer bicycle rentals.

hidden.d: Unusual museum owned by the Lo Heng Mong motorbike shop. In business for more than 50 years, the business has kept an example of most motorcycles they have sold over that period. Most motorcycles are small-displacement scooters.
Guided and self-guided canoe trips in the Kanchanaburi area. Trips can be arranged.
This well-signposted complex houses a bizarre collection of museums and exhibits, most of which are poorly maintained and labelled.

n.en: World War II Museum and Art Gallery

hidden.d: A modern day spa set amidst lush tropical gardens beside the tranquil River Kwai (next to bridge). Spa facilities consist of 16 beds with private rooms, guest showers, and trained therapists.

This is the final resting place of 6,982 POWs who gave their lives for the construction of the Death Railway to Burma. All POWs at this site are from the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Australia.
A neatly maintained small cemetery 2 km out of town.
Generally considered to be the best source of information regarding World War II in Thailand, railway construction and route, and the conditions endured by POWs and Asian labourers.

x.intro: Kanchanaburi (Thai: กาญจนบุรี) is a city at the confluence of the Rivers Kwai Noi and Kwai Yai.

must.d: Formerly called Khao Salop National Park (อุทยานแห่งชาติเขาสลอบ), it was proclaimed a national park on 19 June 1975, with an area of 373,735 rai (597,976,000 m2).
Contenders for the most beautiful waterfalls in Thailand, and a must-see if time and budget allow. The falls are composed of seven tiers, all of which are picturesque and great for swimming.
The acronym JEATH stands for the primary nationalities involved in the construction of the railway: Japanese, English, Australian, American, Thai and Holland.

next.d: most visitors get out where they came from
the world's largest stupa makes a good pitstop along the way to Bangkok
last town before the Three Pagodas Pass border crossing into Myanmar
the border between Thailand and Myanmar, 4 hours away by bus

cities.d: (นครราชสีมา) — largest city of the Isaan region, also known as Khorat.

x.around: Happily, the reputation that tuk-tuk drivers have for ripping off tourists in places like Phuket and Pattaya does not generally apply in Korat. The fare from the main bus station to Yamo/city centre is 60 baht. Agree on this price before you get in. Fares typically go up in multiples of 20 and start at 40 baht.
x.intro: Nakhon Ratchasima (นครราชสีมา), usually referred to as Khorat (โคราช) or, more commonly Korat, is the largest city in the Isaan region of Thailand. Its proximity to Bangkok makes it a good jumping-off point for travellers who are heading into further into the region. It has excellent transport links to the rest of the country and beyond.

next.d: largest national park of Thailand with fascinating animals, waterfalls and more
the historical Khmer remains
amazing temple right on the border with Cambodia, no separate visa necessary to visit
the annual elephant parade
and Rongkleu Market — border crossing to Cambodia. There are 7 buses daily from the new bus station to Rongkluea market (05:30, 08:00, 10:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00 and 18:00).

cities.d: (พัทยา) — one of the main tourist destinations, known for its wild nightlife

x.around: Flat fares only apply when operating as a bus. Beware of the driver of an otherwise empty songthaew, especially one that's parked at the roadside, who might presume (or decide on your behalf) that you want to charter him as a taxi, in which case expect a much higher fare, depending on your negotiating skills. Taxis in Pattaya do not use meters at all.

hidden.d: A park at the foot of Khao Pattaya. With an area of 6 acres, the park was dedicated to commemorate His Majesty the King's sixtieth birthday on 5 Dec 1988.

This is an “illusion” art museum that features ten galleries – the Camouflage Room, Under the Ocean Room, Wildlife Room, Classical Art Room, Civilization Room, Surrealism Room, Dinosaur Room, Waterfall Room, Scenery Room, and…

This elephant camp focuses on the daily lives of elephants and their keepers and also offers stage shows demonstrating how to catch wild elephants, elephants-at-work in the jungle, elephants playing football, and a grand war…
Inside the farm are various kinds of orchids to be admired and purchased such as Pompadua, Vanda, Golden Shower, and Cattleya.
Directly after the show the performers come outside for a few minutes photo session.
This small tranquil 1 kilometre beach is on the north side of Pattaya Bay. The serene atmosphere here is attractive to those longing for a complete rest and privacy.

Tiffany's is a family-friendly ladyboy cabaret show. The 19:30 show is generally deemed to be the best of the night. After the show there the ladyboys would gather outside available for photos sessions with interested audience.

x.intro: Pattaya (พัทยา) is a seaside resort on the Eastern Gulf Coast of Thailand, about 150 km southeast of Bangkok. Pattaya is mostly famous for its go-go and beer bars, but local authorities have made some efforts to provide more family-friendly attractions and activities. Although the sex industry is still going strong, Pattaya also attracts domestic and international tourists.

must.d: This huge ancient-style wooden temple is by the sea at Laem Ratchawet, north Pattaya. The entrance is at Soi 12, Na Kluea Rd. The Sanctuary of Truth was first begun in 1981 by Mr.
Buddha Hill is one of the highest points in Pattaya. At the summit is the biggest Buddha statue in Pattaya, and nearby is a beautiful Chinese-style sacred area dedicated to Confucius and Lao-zi.

next.d: see what Thais do at the beach
one of the local festivals like the Buffalo Race may justify a day trip
officially a part of Pattaya, this beach front is more mellow and popular among families and expats
small island close to Pattaya
small island just north of Ko Laan
quiet white beaches
small nearby island, not focused on beach life

x.safe: Most accidents in Pattaya involve motorbikes, and are especially common late at night and in the early hours of the morning, when drunk driving is a significant problem. Be careful on the roads, even if you're just crossing one on foot (and be equally careful both on and off pedestrian crossings, as Thai drivers generally ignore them, and many foreigners seem to approach them with the hope of scoring double points);…

cities.d: (สุโขทัย) — Thailand's first capital, still with amazing ruins

x.around: It's an easy 15-minute walk from the into New Sukothai town along a dirt path in front of the bus station (although the tuk tuk drivers will tell you that it is not possible to walk). To find it, exit the front of the station and walk straight (west) for a few meters until you reach the shops in front of the station. There will be the leading off to your left (south) that passes by some fields and houses.

hidden.d: Just north of the central zone, the Wat Phra Phai Lung group of monuments stands on an area surrounded by a moat 600 m long on each side.

Wat Si Chum complex is north west of the central zone and south west of Wat Phra Phai Luang. It is known for its giant Buddha statue known as Phra Achana (Buddha who is not afraid) and Phra Poot Dai (speaking Buddha).

The giant statue of King Ramkhamhaeng stands almost at the centre of the Sukhothai Historical Park. King Ramkamhaeng ruled Sukhothai between 1279 and 1298 and was the third king of the Phra Ruang Dynasty, approximately.
It is the remains of the royal palace of the Kingdom of Sukhothai. The palace was built on a square base with the dimensions of 200 x 200 m.

x.intro: Sukhothai (สุโขทัย) is a small city (population 14,000 in 2019) in Lower Northern Thailand, 427 km north of Bangkok. Its attraction lies in the ruins of the ancient city Sukhothai, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The name translates as "the dawn of happiness".

must.d: It is one of the oldest temples in Sukhothai. The temple was founded in the late-12th or early-13th century as a Hindu Shrine for Vishnu and the place for the Thiruppavai ceremony before the liberation from Lawo and foundation of…
It is the most important temple of the Sukhothai Historical Park. The temple's name translates to temple of the great relic.

Located almost at the centre of the central complex, Wat Sa Si is on an island surrounded by a man made lake, known as Tra Phang Tra Kuan. It is located west of King Ramkhamhaeng Monument and north west of Wat Maha That.
Built in 14th century the name literally translates into Silver Lake Temple. The temple consists of a giant lotus bud chedi (stupa) along with a smaller chedi and an assembly hall.
Wat Chetuphon is the most impressive of the southern zone. Literally meaning Temple of the Divine General it stands 1.6 km south of the South Gate (Namo Gate).
Wat Si Phichit Kirati Kanlayaram literally meaning Temple of the Glorious, Honorable, and Beautiful Building is about 800 m south east of Wat Chedi Si Hong.

Wat Chang Lom is about 500 m east of the East Gate (Kamphaeng Hak Gate) and about 100 m north of the main road. Like Wat Sorasak, which is located inside the central zone, Wat Chang Lom also consists of 32 elephants along its…

next.d: historic town
Sukhothai's twin city
Despite two large signs detailing​ explicitly the bus schedule with class and prices, 3 different bus companies (WinTour, Transport and another one) explained us that no 2nd class buses are running…
For 230 baht from the bus station you can take a bus. First in the morning is 6h30.
to the Myanmar border. Minibuses leave the Sukhothai Bus Station 09:15, 10:15,14:15 & 16:15 (3½hr travel time) ฿196 (Jan 2020)
there are government buses at 13h, 15h and 18h

intro: Thailand (Thai: ประเทศไทย Prathet Thai or เมืองไทย Mueang Thai) is among the most visited countries on Earth, and for good reason. You can find thick jungle as green as can be, crystal blue waters that feel more like a warm bath than a swim in the ocean, and food that can curl your nose hairs while tap dancing across your taste buds.

other.d: (Thai: เขาสก) — one of the most beautiful wildlife reserves in Thailand

x.around: Walking is the primary mode of transportation, as the road to the park is 2 km and the farthest one can walk into the park is about 20 km.

hidden.d: Waterfall flowing along the cliff in layers that looks like the stairs of 11 steps. At the bottom, there is a pool for swimming. It is accessible on foot.
Small, 100m long cave with stalactites. Easily accessible. Located on Klong Ka.
Namtok Ton Kloi originates from Khlong Sok. It is a one-tiered waterfall with a stony ground for visitors to take a rest beside it. It is about 9 km from the Park's headquarters.

Small limestone cave temple. Friendly monkeys live alongside the temple and on the hill. Note: The monkeys get easily scared by loud noises, so you might not be able to see them the day after a large thunder storm or a fireworks…
Popular for rafting activities, this waterfall with small rapids is 3km from the visitor center.
A 500 m long cave with water streaming through it. It's a 4 km hike to reach the cave. Located on Klong Pey. The cave is very dangerous on rainy days.
An eco-tourism elephant sanctuary program and family run cooking class. The 2-hour program is run twice daily.

n.en: Khao Sok National Park Visitor Center

x.intro: Khao Sok National Park (pronounced "cow soak") is a jungle reserve in Southern Thailand. It is one of the most beautiful wildlife reserves in Thailand.
x.safe: Do not explore the "Namtaloo" or "Through" Cave (a cave with a river running through) if it is raining or if you think it is going to rain. Rain is frequent and can come on fast. Unfortunately people have died as a result of this. If you are with an experienced guide he will not take you if he even suspects a chance of rain.

other.d: (Thai: เขาใหญ่) — take a night time Jeep safari spotting deer or visit the spectacular waterfalls

x.around: One of the best ways to see the park is renting a car or motorbike in Pak Chong and staying one night in the park. If you don't have your own transport it is quite difficult to get to the park information centre as the bus from Pak Chong usually takes you to the ticket office and the natural park centre is about 10 km away.
x.intro: Khao Yai National Park is a national park in Southern Isaan, Thailand.
x.safe: Do not swim in the rivers and waterfalls, there may be crocodiles.

other.d: (Thai: เกาะช้าง) — once a quiet island, now undergoing major tourism development

x.around: The only form of public transportation on Ko Chang is the songtaew. There are about 90 licenced songtaews whose drivers form a co-op. They have a rostering system that ensures equal access to the pier so all drivers receive a fair share of the lucrative fares from piers to accommodation. This means that shorter fares along the west coast are more expensive per kilometre than fares from the pier.

hidden.d: The most popular waterfall, and the only one on the west side of the island.
A renovation is underway at the memorial site, with a huge building being constructed (Jan 2018).
By far the busiest as it is the first beach visitors reach when they arrive on the island.
Waterfall on the east side of the island. Reachable by foot from the Klong Plu waterfall, 6 km.
The village temple of Ban Salak Phet, built in the reign of King Rama V on his visit to the island. The original temple is now used as a museum commemorating the king's visits to the area.

x.intro: Ko Chang (เกาะช้าง) is an island in Trat Province, Eastern Thailand. It is the third biggest island in Thailand (after Phuket and Ko Samui)

other.d: (Thai: เกาะหลีเป๊ะ) — small island in the middle of Tarutao National Park, with great reefs and beaches

x.around: All of Ko Lipe can be covered on foot. A walk between the two furthest walkable points on the island, Serendipity Resort and Patai Galah Beach, takes about 45 minutes for the 3 km journey, using the roads. There are many motorcycles on the island, although none of them are for rent.

hidden.d: Experienced instructors teaching all PADI courses from beginner to divemaster level. Daily trips for certified divers to all the best dive sites around Ko Lipe.

Ko Lipe Diving is a SSI Diamond Dive Center and Instructor Training Facility. They offer daily fun dive day trips for certified divers, a full range of SSI courses from beginner to pro, introductory dives (you can try Scuba…

x.intro: Ko Lipe (Thai: เกาะหลีเป๊ะ) (sometimes spelled Koh Lipe) is an island in Satun Province, off the Andaman Coast of Southern Thailand. It is 50km northwest of Langkawi, Malaysia, 67km west of Pak Bara, and 200km southeast of Phuket. It is part of a cluster of islands called the Butang / Adang Archipelago.

other.d: (Thai: เกาะพะงัน) — site of the famous Full Moon Party with miles of quiet coastline

x.around: There are many rental locations all over the island. They have formed an association and all have the same prices, saying this should prevent the problems with the scams that many people complained about before. The advertised price is now 250 baht/day, can be bargained to 200 baht/day if renting for more days, but basically impossible to get anything cheaper.
x.intro: Ko Pha-ngan (เกาะพะง้น, , pronounced KOH pa-NGan with NG as in bringing) is an island off the Central Gulf Coast of Southern Thailand and forms part of the Chumphon Archipelago. Halfway between the islands of Ko Samui and Ko Tao, it is known as a land of coconut trees and the world-famous Full Moon Party that have placed the island firmly on the Banana Pancake Trail.

next.d: 2 hours away by boat and a great place for a day-trip only (snorkelling, swimming, kayaking, viewpoint over 42 islands) through travel agencies, not on your own. There are huts and tents available.

the biggest and most touristy island (on the east coast) of Thailand, many boats departing for there from 250 baht.
"the biggest dive school on the planet" (Songserm express ferry leaving Thong Sala at 12:30 for 250 baht).
closest city on the mainland.

x.safe: Yes, the Full Moon Party (as well as others) is full of drugs, but these days it's also full of plain clothed policemen out to bust you. Be very careful if you intend to consume illicit drugs. Roadblocks are common, particularly in the week before the FMP between Thong Sala and Haad Rin. Thai police have also been known to force urine tests.

other.d: (Thai: เกาะเสม็ด) — the nearest island beach escape from Bangkok

x.around: The island is very small in comparison to the more populated Thai islands, so exploring the island can easily be done on foot, bike, or by hiring a motorbike and driving down the island to visit a few of the smaller more secluded beaches and taking in some of the more naturally forested areas further down to the south of the island. ATVs are no longer available on the island.

hidden.d: Some like this beach for being laid back and less developed, with a bit of a feel of the old Thailand. Others find it scruffy, and feel it can get pretty dirty and some have complained about oily sand (?).

This is a private beach because the only way to access it is via the large and exclusive Paradee Resort. Walking along the coast is possible but tricky. It is a lovely spacious beach with trees dotted around.
A perfect hideaway for holidaymakers in search of tranquillity. Only one type of accommodation here: handmade bungalows with a lot of character. Few dining options.
Shaded by coconut trees, the beach is quiet & scenic. There is a jetty here for ferries, so the usual pros and cons apply. Confusingly also called Wai Beach.
Shaded by trees and with space above the high tide line, the beach is quiet & scenic. Access is through resort which dominates beach but not controlled.
A large bay where lots of sport activities such as fishing take place.

Functionally this is a private beach because the only way to access it is via the large Nimmanoradee Resort. The beach has good snorkelling but not good enough to itself justify staying at this resort.

x.intro: Ko Samet (เกาะเสม็ด), also spelled Koh Samed, is a small island off the Eastern Gulf Coast in Rayong province, within easy reach of Bangkok and Pattaya.

less-visited island, again with sandy beaches
virtually no night life, but a very relaxed atmosphere
den of sleaze trying to clean up its act
the beaches near Ranong are known for their decent surfing

x.around: As on many islands in Thailand, small motorbikes are available for rental. Compared to other nearby islands, Samui's road system is very developed and there are plenty of taxis cruising about, although it's a challenge to get them to use their meters.

hidden.d: Has a 15 m tall statue of the Buddha. It was built in 1972.

The undersea world of the aquarium has an amazing collection of tropical fish and other vibrant aquatic animals such as turtles and colourful coral. The tiger zoo is home to Bengal tigers and leopards.
Easily accessible by car. Some of the numerous tiny levels have a large basin for swimmers.
A local road leads to the Na Mueang 1 Waterfall just off Rte 4169. A walk of about 30 minutes ends up at the more scenic Na Mueang 2 Waterfall.
These odd-looking rocks at the south end of Lamai Beach bear a striking resemblance to male and female genitalia and they have turned into one of the island’s biggest attractions.
This chedi (pagoda) at Laem Sor temple is one of the most important shrines on Ko Samui. The structure with its yellow tiles which gives off a golden aura is quite impressive.
This village grows high quality fruits, including rambutan, durian, mangosteen and the famed langsat.

x.intro: Ko Samui (เกาะสมุย), often called just Samui (สมุย) is an island of great natural beauty and variety in the Gulf of Thailand. The palm-fringed shoreline and coconut and fruit cultivation of the coastal lowlands rise to a central granite massif, the slopes of which are cloaked in virgin rainforest.

x.safe: Tap water is not potable. Liquids from sealed bottles nearly always are, and should be used wherever possible. Restaurants buy ice made from purified water, so don’t worry about ice. Tap water in most hotels should not be used for drinking or brushing teeth unless explicitly labelled as safe.

x.around: Phuket is a large island and you need some form of transport to get around. Luckily, there are a variety of transport options for various budgets. Hotels generally offer shuttle bus services into Phuket Town, and also have taxi and car hire facilities.
x.intro: Phuket (ภูเก็ต), pronounced (roughly) "puh-KET", is Thailand's largest island. It is 48 km in length, 21 km at its widest, and is in Southern Thailand, on the west-facing Andaman Sea coastline, suspended from the southern tip of Phang Nga province by a pair of short but substantial road bridges.

x.safe: Particularly in the summer monsoon season, there are strong currents on many of the beaches and drownings are a depressingly common occurrence. Four tourists died during a single 3-day stretch in June 2009. Heed the warning flags on popular beaches and play it safe if off the beaten track.
